text.p: Following are the main stories in today's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The ruling national front has won the Semerak constituency byelection for the state legislature in northern Kelantan state, which is ruled by an opposition party.
-- The government may impose high import tax to reduce the country's growing current account deficit, according to Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar.
-- Civil servants who opt to continue with their respective agencies after their corporatised will get the benefits of working in the private sector as well as retain perks of a government employee.

-- Investments by Malaysians overseas should surpass last year's total after a sharp rise in the first five months of the year. In the January to May period, Malaysia's investments reached 3.56 billion ringgit, more than half of 1996 full year total of 6.85 billion ringgit.
